analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md, so no executable security behavior changes. The base excerpt (lines 1619-1764) and the head excerpt (lines 1-415) were reviewed. The patch excerpt shows three documentation additions: head lines 619-625 on out-of-order performance observations and `EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate` freshness; 869-905 on TTFT admission estimator corrections and the `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0` rollback; and a change at 1767 (path update at base 1723). The patch excerpt is truncated and the head text covers only lines 1-415, so the full set of added lines was not visible. The excerpt did not show the code behind these descriptions, so none of the documented behavior was verified.

The visible head text, a Nemotron Super description, restates existing bounds: media and video charges, ingress limits, LOAD claim admission, and per-scope prefix cache partitioning. It describes prefix reuse within an authenticated tenant scope, with image requests lacking a scope staying cold and never publishing. This matches the T-041 posture (coordinator-authored scope, SEC-035 accepted risk) and introduces no new at-rest artifact or relaxed gate. The documented DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_* and TTFT estimator environment variables are operator-local knobs. Descriptions of performance-evidence freshness relate to capacity and routing claims, not to authorization (TB-011) or attestation.

No threat model assumptions are invalidated by documentation alone. Remaining questions for integration: whether the code behind the estimator and Rate-freshness changes was altered in other batches, and whether the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES rollback switch could enable admission of work beyond deadlines. That would be an availability question under T-010/T-029.
